questions.stem: A set has 4 elements, q0, q1, q2 and q3. How many subsets does it have, counting the empty set and the whole set?
questions.explain: Each element is either in or out, so there are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16 subsets.

questions.stem: The universe is the 4 strings ε (empty string), a, aa and aaa. A set L contains a and aaa. How many strings are in the complement of L?
questions.explain: The complement is everything in the universe that is not in L, which is ε and aa. That is 2 strings.

questions.stem: Set P has 10 strings, set R has 7 strings, and 4 strings are in both. How many strings are in P or R (or both)?
questions.explain: Add the sizes and subtract the overlap once: 10 + 7 − 4 = 13.

questions.stem: Which statement is equivalent to NOT (p OR q)?
questions.explain: De Morgan's law: pushing NOT inside flips OR to AND, so NOT (p OR q) = (NOT p) AND (NOT q).

questions.stem: When is the statement "if p then q" false?
options: Only when p is true and q is false
Whenever p and q are both true
questions.explain: An implication is broken only by a case where the condition holds but the conclusion fails. If p is false, the statement is true by default.

questions.stem: What is the negation of "every string in L has length at most 3"?
options: Some string in L has length at most 3
Some string in L has length greater than 3
Every string in L has length greater than 3
No string in L has length at most 3
questions.explain: Negating a "for all" statement gives "there exists", and the condition inside is negated: at most 3 becomes greater than 3.
